records.title: AVIC Systems Split — 2010 Newspaper Original
records.author_org: Actual original describes 2010 division into avionics/electromechanical businesses; private and listed entities distinguished
records.type: The supplied PDF p.141, note 1019, and each named original were individually assessed. Both named newspaper works were read. The exact printed 2018 route returns 404; its same-publisher migrated edition was recovered. The 2010 account explicitly describes that year’s split, while the September 2018 account describes formation by merger. The actual later issuer financial-adviser disclosure further specifies that the private avionics limited company was to be absorbed and deregistered, with the surviving company inheriting its rights and obligations. The report’s suggestion that both private entities simply continued independently must be distinguished from the separately listed joint-stock companies with similar English names. Correct that legal-entity ambiguity; these accounts do not mean a listed-company merger completed in 2018.

The 2003 rule, Article 28, allows rectification or cancellation after a failed assessment; it does not guarantee every failing laboratory a rectification interval. Article 30 of the 2009 revision distinguishes a basically qualified result requiring rectification from an unqualified result requiring cancellation. The report’s generalized account needs those alternatives and edition qualifiers. Its subsequent inference of lax enforcement also requires an adequate record of assessments and withdrawals, rather than deriving enforcement practice from the rule alone. Current applicability and the empirical enforcement record remain open. Article 19 of the 2003 text gives an ordinary committee ceiling of 15, or 20 for a joint laboratory, rather than a universal 15–20 membership range. Its three-year term, parent-institution one-third ceiling and one-third replacement rule match the older edition. The 2009 revision’s Articles 17–18 retain the parent-share limit but change the term to five years and use a ceiling of 20. The report combines an overbroad membership range with an older term and should identify which historical edition it describes. The applicable current instrument and actual laboratory appointments remain unresolved; the later university posting date must not be mistaken for a new enactment. Article 3 of the historical text reproduced by Yanshan University supports the quoted institutional research mission. Article 30 expressly gives January 20, 2003 as its effective date, despite the university page’s inconsistent 2011 heading and 2020 posting date. The exact cited Hunan route is unavailable. The report explicitly introduces this as the 2003 guideline, so the dated quotation is supported. A separate 2009 revision, reproduced by Yangtze University, repeals that version; this finding does not certify the 2003 rule as current in 2025. The two editions prescribe different processes. The 2003 text distinguishes applications needing new construction investment from those already qualified and describes a construction period generally not exceeding two years. Articles 9–10 of the 2009 revision instead provide trial operation and an assessment application within two years. The report’s roughly two-year probation account resembles the latter, although its repeated citation points to the older text. A deadline is also not an observed typical duration. The procedural edition and actual-duration evidence remain unresolved; the source does not justify treating every laboratory as following an identical waiting period. The 2003 text’s Articles 2 and 15 support a leading civilian-agency role and its approval of directors, but name COSTIND and the General Armaments Department. The recovered 2009 revision instead names SASTIND and the GAD and retains civilian approval of directors. The report acknowledges later institutional successors in its own note viii. These records support historical arrangements, while the exact transfer of each responsibility to the contemporary Equipment Development Department still needs a dated authoritative record. The regulation’s prescribed division of responsibilities does not measure actual day-to-day influence. The same historical Article 3 explicitly includes an advanced open research platform, civil–military combination and dual-use development. This supports the report’s second attributed quotation as a rendering of the 2003 text. It is a prescribed mission, not evidence that every laboratory achieved the specified standard. The later revision and the university reposting dates are kept distinct; a current institutional conclusion requires current rules and implementation evidence.

Seven individually read passages retain their specific access or interpretation gaps. A distinct 360inno companion in notes 168/182 is separately indexed, and duplicated printed number 182 is explicitly preserved as an original-document ambiguity. The individually marked passage at supplied PDF p.83 was compared with its complete original citation. The cited NWPU page is 403 and its original body was not recovered. The separately read August 28, 2022 university departmental history gives a 1995 low-speed-tunnel construction statement and a national third-class award, whereas the directory gives 1994 completion and a 1994 first-class aviation award. These may involve distinct milestones and award systems; they are not automatically the same award or proof that either whole account is false. The exact 1988 approval, 1994 milestone and award record need the original 2013 article or dated acceptance instruments. Laboratory establishment, tunnel construction, operational commissioning and award year remain separate events. The individually marked passage at supplied PDF p.87 was compared with its complete original citation. The named software, first-export assertion and the report’s malformed on-structural wording remain unverified pending their original Chinese context and historical edition. Related departmental research descriptions do not authenticate a particular software export or demonstrate performance. No design software, algorithms or engineering methods were reconstructed. The individually marked passage at supplied PDF p.87 was compared with its complete original citation. The historical claim that AVIC assisted construction of NF-6 depends on the unavailable 2013 university article. A newer joint-laboratory relationship or a current AVIC association cannot establish who funded, commissioned or built the earlier tunnel. No dated agreement, construction account or funding instrument was recovered for this precise attribution. The source’s historical group name and the report’s CAVIC rendering also need the original wording rather than an assumed modern corporate identity. This leaves a specific institutional-history gap, without assessing tunnel engineering. The individually marked passage at supplied PDF p.88 was compared with its complete original citation. A separately indexed university teaching slide is consistent with parts of the NF-3 section layout, but its full original PDF was not recovered and it is not the cited 2013 edition. The exact translated specification set, measurement date and ancillary-room assertion therefore remain open; no tunnel configuration or engineering verification procedure was compiled. The individually marked passage at supplied PDF p.89 was compared with its complete original citation. The unavailable 2013 source prevents checking the exact NF-6 specification and milestone wording. The separately read 2022 university history distinguishes 2003 construction from completion of commissioning/debugging in 2008. The report instead says commissioned in 2000 and finished in 2003 in its preceding equipment entry; commissioned could be an order rather than operational acceptance and needs clarification against the original. The historical start-of-use paragraph and the exact cited specification context remain needed. The individually marked passage at supplied PDF p.89 was compared with its complete original citation. The only cited original page is unavailable. A facility’s stated research purpose, even if later recovered, would not by itself establish an accomplished engine result or national exclusivity. records.title: Sunway TaihuLight — Contributor Repost
records.author_org: Jianshu contributor 浩浩_72a 0; identifies an earlier repost source, not a benchmark log
records.type: The supplied PDF p.150, full note 467 and particular cited passage were individually checked. Both actual cited bodies were read. The Jianshu item is a contributor repost, while the recovered Tsinghua page republishes He Liang’s August 1, 2017 Science and Technology Daily report; neither is a primary benchmark log. That article does give the report’s 16,384-processor, one-eighth, 20-day/12-month comparison, so the copied numbers are traceable. However, the actual TOP500 system record, including its 2017 row, lists 10,649,600 cores and 260 cores per processor, implying 40,960 processors; 16,384 is 40 percent of that count, not one eighth. Flag the inherited denominator/unit conflict and seek the original experiment’s resource definition rather than silently changing its benchmark. Keep the timing as an attributed reported comparison, not independently measured performance. The standard English system name is Sunway TaihuLight, not Shineway.
